hook.text: A coin flip is 50-50, but it can land heads ten times in a row. Markets work the same—randomness fools everyone.

buildup.text: Every trade has an uncertain outcome. Even the best setups fail sometimes. Certainty doesn't exist in trading.

discovery.text: Probabilistic thinking means accepting that each trade is one data point in a large sample. Results vary.

twist.text: Most people think in certainties: 'This trade will work.' Experts think: 'This trade has a 60% chance.' Big difference.

climax.text: When you truly accept uncertainty, losses stop being personal. They become expected events within your model.

quiz.question: What does thinking in probabilities mean?
options: Accepting uncertainty and viewing each trade as one sample in a larger set
